comment: The missed B/E tradeoff was bundled architecture, not activation alone: B's wide residual GELU block optimized better than E's deeper but plain LeakyReLU stack at this very low Adam rate. C's deeper residual composition and two LNs best fit the 1.5-turn boundary; A's two-LN rectifier follows. I over-applied smooth-activation and LayerNorm tendencies across unequal residual/depth bundles. K1008 and K1020 were misleading when used as cross-architecture tie-breaks; K1015/K1016's cautions and the matching q_3eeb02 history supported treating depth, width, and skips jointly.
hypothesis: A scoped rule for 1–2-turn spirals under 256 steps and Adam around 3e-5: rank by effective boundary-learning capacity, where residual pathways and width can outweigh one extra plain hidden block, while additional depth plus residual composition dominates when accompanied by at least one extra LN. Do not transfer activation-only preferences across residual/depth changes. This predicts C (deep residual, 2 LN) > A (2 LN rectifier) > B (wide shallow residual) > E (deeper plain Leaky) > D (deep plain SiLU, sparse LN). Backtest: the historical matching spiral record q_3eeb02 had the same gold order, 1/1 hit; broader history showed reversals, so this remains a narrow, falsifiable heuristic rather than a universal architecture law.
